### Shape

#### Description

The Application tab of the ribbon, last of the tabs.

#### Groups

```
appearance: An "Appearance" group holds the Brightness command, its one control; there is no Dark mode switch, since the slider reaches both modes.
colours: A "Colours" group, between Appearance and Preferences, holds the Theme command.
preferences: A "Preferences" group holds the Settings command.
```

#### Commands

```
brightness: A "Brightness" slider, which runs the whole interface from its darkest to its lightest: a moon icon, then a horizontal slider 120 pixels wide, then a sun icon, with nothing showing the setting as a number. As a ribbon setting, it has no background of its own, and sits straight on the commands' area, as tall as a slim button. Its tooltip says it makes the whole interface darker or lighter, from its darkest to its lightest, keeping its contrast, and that double-clicking it resets it.
  Its one track runs through every appearance the [ThemeScope](../../../theme/index.md#theme-scope) allows, darkest first: dark mode from its darkest brightness to its lightest, then light mode from its darkest to its lightest, one position for each step, with no switch between them. So all the way left is dark mode at its darkest, and all the way right light mode at its lightest; dragging past dark mode's lightest step changes the window to light mode, and back.
  Dragging it changes the mode and the brightness straight away as it moves, and once it is let go saves the mode showing and each mode's brightness among the [UserPreferencesScope](../../../../scope/user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope). A mode that can't be saved shows a notification titled "Could not save brightness", with why; a brightness that can't be saved fails quietly. Its thumb follows the appearance showing, however that was changed, such as from the palette, but not while it is being dragged.
  Double-clicking anywhere on it, its icons or its track, puts the mode showing back to its brightness at 0, keeping the mode, and saves it; the second click doesn't also move the thumb.
  It is primary, so the collapsed ribbon keeps it: its icons and track as they are, only as wide as they are, as tall as a small button.
theme: A "Theme" button with a palette icon. Clicking it opens the [ThemeEditorScope](../../theme-editor/index.md#theme-editor-scope). Its tooltip says it chooses the base colour, and the colours of Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask.
  It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon leaves it out.
settings: A "Settings" button with a gear icon. Clicking it opens the [SettingsWindowScope](../../../../scope/settings-window/index.md#settings-window-scope), where the system prompt each chat tab sends is edited. Its tooltip says so, and gives its keyboard shortcut, Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS).
  It is primary, and a full button.
```
### Shape

#### Description

Until a [ProjectDirectoryScope](../project-directory/index.md#project-directory-scope) is open, nothing that needs one does anything, or fails for want of one.

#### Views

Something that shows the project's things shows, in place of them, a short message saying no project is open, or what to open one for. Each use gives its words.

#### Commands

A command that needs a project is disabled, not hidden, with a tooltip saying to open a project to do what the command does. Each use gives its words.

#### Opening

As soon as a project opens, each comes to life by itself.

### Shape

#### Description

The panel floats over everything in the window, the ribbon and sidebar included, inset 32 pixels from every edge of the window. It has rounded corners, a border, and a shadow, and whatever it holds fills it. The window behind it is dimmed, and nothing behind it takes the mouse while it is open. Only one panel is open at a time.

#### Animating

The panel comes in each time it opens and goes away each time it closes with the [RiseInAnimation](../../animations/rise-in/index.md#rise-in-animation): the panel is its surface, and the dimmed window around the panel is its dimming. Switching what the panel holds, such as opening a diff while the settings are open, swaps it in place.

#### Modal

While the panel is open, nothing beneath it can take focus or input; only the panel and what it holds can.
The mouse can't reach anything beneath: no clicks, scrolling, hovering, or tooltips, except that clicking the dimmed window closes the panel.
Focus moves into the panel when it opens and can't leave it. <Tab> and <Shift+Tab> cycle through what can be focused within the panel, going round from the last back to the first and the other way, rather than on to anything beneath. Anything that would move focus beneath while it is open, such as a task beneath finishing, sends focus back into the panel instead.
The main window's shortcuts that act on what is beneath do nothing while it is open: opening the palette with <Ctrl+P> (<Cmd+P> on macOS), and collapsing or expanding the ribbon with <Ctrl+F1> (<Cmd+F1> on macOS). Shortcuts that open something of their own, like the settings window, or quitting, still work.

#### Closing

The panel closes with a close or cancel button in what it holds, with <Escape>, or by clicking the dimmed window around it; clicking inside the panel never closes it. Once it closes, focus goes back to the chat input.

export ui-component WelcomeScope:
    concept: {WelcomeConcept}

concept WelcomeConcept:
    pitch:
        A welcome page that checks what Suspense needs is installed and
        working, says plainly what isn't, and guides each fix, so Suspense
        is ready before the first prompt is sent rather than failing on it.

    shape: {WelcomeShape}

shape WelcomeShape:
    description:
        Shown in an @{InsetPanelScope}, as the settings are, headed "Welcome
        to Suspense", with a close button whose tooltip says it closes the
        welcome page. Beneath the heading, a muted line says that Suspense
        runs coding harnesses on a project's code and spec, and checks here
        that what it needs is in place. Then a checklist, one row per check,
        in order, and at its foot a "Check again" button, and a line saying
        whether Suspense is ready.

    checks:
        Each check is a row: a status icon, a green check when it passes, a
        red cross when a required check fails, an amber warning when an
        optional one does, and a spinner while it is being checked; the
        check's name; muted beside it what was found, as the version a
        command reports; and, beneath, while it fails, a line of guidance
        saying what is wrong, why Suspense needs it, and how to fix it, with
        the action that fixes it where Suspense can take one. The checks, in
        order:

        - "Git", found by running `git --version`, required, since projects
          are git repositories. Missing, its guidance links to
          https://git-scm.com/downloads.

export ui-component WelcomeScope:
    concept: {WelcomeConcept}

concept WelcomeConcept:
    pitch:
        A welcome page that checks what Suspense needs is installed and
        working, says plainly what isn't, and guides each fix, so Suspense
        is ready before the first prompt is sent rather than failing on it.

    shape: {WelcomeShape}

shape WelcomeShape:
    description:
        Shown in an @{InsetPanelScope}, as the settings are, headed "Welcome
        to Suspense", with a close button whose tooltip says it closes the
        welcome page. Beneath the heading, a muted line says that Suspense
        runs coding harnesses on a project's code and spec, and checks here
        that what it needs is in place. Then a checklist, one row per check,
        in order, and at its foot a "Check again" button, and a line saying
        whether Suspense is ready.

    checks:
        Each check is a row: a status icon, a green check when it passes, a
        red cross when a required check fails, an amber warning when an
        optional one does, and a spinner while it is being checked; the
        check's name; muted beside it what was found, as the version a
        command reports; and, beneath, while it fails, a line of guidance
        saying what is wrong, why Suspense needs it, and how to fix it, with
        the action that fixes it where Suspense can take one. The checks, in
        order:

        - "Git", found by running `git --version`, required, since projects
          are git repositories. Missing, its guidance links to
          https://git-scm.com/downloads.
        - "Piton", found by running `piton --version`, required, since the
          spec is built, sliced, and checked with it. Missing, its guidance
          links to https://github.com/piton-lang/piton-rs.
        - "Harness", the harness in use, as the @{HarnessIntegrationScope}
          says, found by running its command with `--version`, required,
          since Code tasks run it on the host. Missing, its guidance names the
          command and links to the harness's installation instructions,
          https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/setup for Claude Code,
          https://github.com/openai/codex for Codex, and
          https://opencode.ai/docs/ for OpenCode, with a "Choose another
          harness" button that opens the Agent section of the
          @{SettingsWindowScope}.
        - "Podman", found by running `podman --version`, required, since
          Spec tasks, a Chain prompt's spec steps, and questions run in a
          container, as the @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says. Missing, its
          guidance links to Podman's installation instructions for the
          platform, as it gives them.
        - "Podman machine", on macOS and Windows only, required, passing
          while a Podman machine is running. With none, its guidance offers
          "Set up Podman", and with one stopped, "Start Podman", each as the
          @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says, what the command prints shown
          beneath the row as it runs. It is checked only once Podman is
          found, and shows "Needs Podman", muted, until then.
        - "Containers", required, passing once Podman runs a container for
          the application, as by running `podman info`. Failing, its guidance
          says Podman couldn't be accessed, with what Podman printed, as the
          @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says. It is checked only once the
          checks above it pass.
        - "Harness login", required, passing while the harness in use is
          logged in in its container, read from its volume. Not logged in,
          its guidance offers "Log in", which shows the login view, as the
          @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says. It is checked only once
          "Containers" passes.

        Every check runs in the background, all at once where they don't
        wait on one another, as each command is run without a console
        window, never holding up the window. A command that takes longer
        than 10 seconds fails its check, saying it didn't answer.

    ready:
        Suspense is ready when every required check passes, and the line at
        the checklist's foot then reads "Suspense is ready", with a
        "Get started" button that closes the welcome page; otherwise it
        reads how many checks still need attention, as "2 things need
        attention", and Get started is not shown, the close button closing
        the page all the same, since what passes still works.

        "Check again" runs every check anew. A check whose action, as setting
        up Podman or logging in, finishes runs again by itself, and so do the
        checks waiting on it. A link opened in the browser leaves the page as
        it is, until Check again.

    opening:
        At each launch, Suspense runs the checks in the background as it
        starts. If any required check fails, the welcome page opens over the
        main window once they are done, unless the user has turned off
        "Show at launch when something needs attention", a checkbox at the
        page's foot, on until turned off, remembered for the user. When
        every check passes, nothing is shown.

        It can be opened at any time with the Welcome command, a "Welcome"
        button with a checklist icon in a "Help" group, the last group of the
        @{RibbonApplicationTabScope}, after Preferences, whose tooltip says it
        checks that Suspense is ready to run. It is a full button, and not
        primary, so the collapsed ribbon leaves it out. Opening it runs every
        check anew. It needs no project, and works the same with or without
        one.

content.text:
I've added a Welcome page that checks what Suspense needs, explains what's missing, and opens by itself at launch when something isn't ready. You can reopen it from a new **Welcome** button on the Application tab. `piton check` reports no problems, `piton build` succeeds, and the changed files are formatted. I confirmed the new scope and the ribbon change in the refreshed reference.

**The page:** it opens in the same kind of floating panel as Settings, headed "Welcome to Suspense", with one row per check. Each row shows a pass, fail or warning icon (or a spinner while checking), what was found (such as a version), and, when it fails, what's wrong, why Suspense needs it, and how to fix it.

**The checks, in order** (all required):

| Check | How it's checked | Fix offered |
|---|---|---|
| Git | `git --version` | link to git-scm.com/downloads |
| Piton | `piton --version` | link to github.com/piton-lang/piton-rs |
| Harness (the one picked in Settings) | `<command> --version` | its install page, plus "Choose another harness", which opens Settings → Agent |
| Podman | `podman --version` | Podman's install link for your platform |
| Podman machine (macOS and Windows) | is a machine running | "Set up Podman" or "Start Podman" |
| Containers | `podman info` | says Podman couldn't be accessed, with what Podman printed |
| Harness login | logged in inside its container | "Log in", which opens the existing login view |

Checks that depend on others wait for them. For example, Harness login waits until Containers passes. All checks run in the background without console windows, and a command that doesn't answer within 10 seconds fails its check.

**Ready and rechecking:**
- When every check passes, the foot of the page says "Suspense is ready" with a **Get started** button. Otherwise it says how many things need attention.
- **Check again** reruns everything. Finishing a fix, such as starting Podman or logging in, reruns that check and the ones waiting on it.

**When it appears:**
- At each launch, the checks run in the background. The page opens only if a required check fails, unless you've turned off "Show at launch when something needs attention".
- The **Welcome** button sits in a new last group, "Help", on the Application tab. Opening the page always reruns the checks, and it works with or without a project open.

Choices you may want to change:
- **Required checks:** I marked every check required, so the amber "optional" state exists but nothing uses it yet.
- **Piton link:** it points at github.com/piton-lang/piton-rs, the repository the fluency file mentions. Give me the right URL if there's a better install page.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors still need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings, though nothing here uses them.

## What changed in the spec, and the anchors the code should follow

- **New `spec/scope/welcome/index.pi` (`WelcomeScope`):**
  - **`WelcomeShape.description`:** the floating panel's layout, heading and close button.
  - **`WelcomeShape.checks`:**
    - The seven checks in order, with the command each runs, its dependencies and its fix.
    - Reuse the existing Podman setup and start commands, the login view, and the platform install links from `ContainerEnvironmentScope`. "Choose another harness" opens Settings → Agent.
    - Run checks in the background through the shared no-console process helper, with a 10-second timeout.
  - **`WelcomeShape.ready`:** the ready line and Get started. Check again reruns everything, and a finished fix reruns its check and those waiting on it.
  - **`WelcomeShape.opening`:**
    - Run the checks at launch and open the page if a required check fails and the preference is on. The page's checkbox controls that preference.
    - Opening the page reruns the checks, with or without a project.
- **`RibbonApplicationTabShape.groups.help`** and **`.commands.welcome`:** a last "Help" group holding a full, non-primary "Welcome" button with a checklist icon and the given tooltip.
- **`UserPreferencesShape.preferences`:** add "show the welcome page at launch when something needs attention", which starts on.
